title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: hunt on Microsoft Teams calls and meetings
summary: The briefing's licensing, retention, roadmap facts and access controls are supported. Minor corrections should complete the permissions route and API notes, cite the role-assignment property reference and remove a checklist instruction that has no matching control row.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes security admins with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 hunting on Teams calls and meetings in their organisation.
claims.quote: Security admins with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 can hunt on calls and meetings made inside Microsoft Teams for their organization

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: CallActivityEvents is an advanced hunting table containing activities during Teams calls and meetings in the organisation.
claims.quote: You can hunt across activities performed during Microsoft Teams calls and meetings using the CallActivityEvents advanced hunting table.

claims.claim: The table includes the activity type.
claims.quote: ActivityType | string | Type of activity performed during the call

claims.claim: The table includes activity status.
claims.quote: ActivityStatus | string | Success or failure of the activity performed

claims.claim: The table includes the activity timestamp.
claims.quote: ActivityTimestamp | datetime | Date and time when the activity was recorded

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table includes the activity initiator's user principal name.
claims.quote: ActivityInitiatorUpn | string | User principal name of the participant who initiated the activity

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table includes the activity initiator's display name.
claims.quote: ActivityInitiatorDisplayName | string | Display name of the participant who initiated the activity

claims.claim: The table includes the recipient's account identifier.
claims.quote: ActivityRecipientUpn | string | Unique identifier for the account of the activity recipient

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table includes the initiator's phone number.
claims.quote: ActivityInitiatorPhoneNumber | string | Third-party or Microsoft Teams phone number of the caller's account

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table includes the recipient's phone number.
claims.quote: ActivityRecipientPhoneNumber | string | Third-party or Microsoft Teams phone number of the activity recipient

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table includes the call join URL.
claims.quote: CallJoinUrl | string | Link that participants use to join the call

claims.claim: The table includes the call name.
claims.quote: CallName | string | Name of the call as displayed in the calendar invite

claims.claim: The table includes the call scheduling type.
claims.quote: CallSchedulingType | string | Type of scheduling for the call, such as Adhoc, Scheduled, or Recurring

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table includes the activity initiator's tenant name.
claims.quote: ActivityInitiatorTenantDisplayName | string | Name of the organization that the activity initiator belongs to

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table includes the activity initiator's tenant region.
claims.quote: ActivityInitiatorTenantRegion | string | Geographical region of the tenant that the activity initiator belongs to

claims.claim: The table includes the activity initiator's client platform.
claims.quote: ActivityInitiatorPlatformCategory | string | Category of the activity initiator's client platform; possible values: Desktop, Mobile, Web

claims.claim: Defender for Office 365 supplies the records populating the table.
claims.quote: This advanced hunting table is populated by records from Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Queries do not work or return results unless Defender for Office 365 is deployed in Microsoft Defender.
claims.quote: If your organization hasn't deployed the service in Microsoft Defender, queries that use the table don't work or return any results.

claims.claim: Learn already documents the table in the October 2026 What's new section, despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote:
October 2026
1. Hunt across activities in Microsoft Teams calls and meetings: The CallActivityEvents table in Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting contains details about activities performed during Microsoft Teams calls and meetings in your organization

claims.claim: Microsoft says the table helps security teams investigate suspicious call activity.
claims.quote: helping security teams investigate suspicious call activity.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Advanced hunting queries can be reused to build custom detection rules.
claims.quote: You can use the same threat hunting queries to build custom detection rules.

claims.claim: Custom detection rules run automatically.
claims.quote: These rules run automatically to check for and then respond to suspected breach activity, misconfigured machines, and other findings.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival for this feature, so its default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "CallActivityEvents" "enable" "default"; "Teams calls and meetings" "hunting" "automatically". Read roadmap, CallActivityEvents, Teams support, October What's new and hunting overview; none states this feature's arrival default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Hunting reads the table's call metadata for people with query access.
claims.quote: Queries a specified set of event, activity, or entity data supported by Microsoft 365 Defender to proactively look for specific threats in your environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: Advanced hunting provides up to 30 days of native Defender data by default.
claims.quote: Advanced hunting supports up to 30 days of native Defender data retention by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: An eligible ISOC licence provides up to 90 days for supported Defender data.
claims.quote: With ISOC, customers who have an eligible Microsoft Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5, or Microsoft 365 E7 license receive 90 days of included retention for supported Microsoft Defender data, Azure Activity data, and Office 365 Activity data.

claims.claim: CallActivityEvents is included in the ISOC 90-day retention benefit.
claims.quote:
The following tables and data sources are currently included:
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
CallActivityEvents

claims.claim: The eligible-customer retention benefit starts November 15, 2026.
claims.quote: Starting November 15, 2026, eligible customers receive up to 90 days of included retention for supported Microsoft Defender data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn describe no automated action on calls or end-user behaviour change for this hunting-table item.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: The Teams protection page publishes no separate price or meter for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com "CallActivityEvents" "price" "meter". Read the entire Teams support page and ISOC billing/retention page; Teams support gives plan entitlements, not a separate price or meter for call hunting.

claims.claim: The hunting overview gives a result-set quota of 100,000 rows per query.
claims.quote: Result set | 100,000 rows | Every query | Each query can return up to 100,000 records.

claims.claim: The hunting overview gives a 10-minute query timeout.
claims.quote: Timeout | 10 minutes | Every query | Each query can run for up to 10 minutes. If it doesn't complete within 10 minutes, the service displays an error.

claims.claim: Microsoft Defender portal > Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions reaches role permission selection.
claims.quote:
On the Permissions page, under Microsoft Defender XDR, select Roles > Create custom role.
On the Choose permissions page, select each of the following as needed to configure permissions for that area:
claims.fix: The path correctly reaches the permissions page but stops before the documented hunting permission. Extend it to 'Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions > Security operations > Raw data > Email & collaboration metadata (read)', citing the already-listed https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-overview for the last levels. Preserve the qualification that its explicit table list does not name CallActivityEvents.

claims.claim: POST /beta/roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments creates a Defender provider role assignment.
claims.quote:
To create role assignment for a Defender provider:
POST /roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint. Add to controls[0].note the properties already described in the body: 'The request body sets roleDefinitionId for the assigned role and principalIds for the assigned users or groups.'

claims.claim: The Defender role-assignment endpoint uses the beta Microsoft Graph API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The Defender provider role-assignment API requires RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender.
claims.quote:
For Defender provider
Delegated (work or school account) | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender
Application | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender

claims.claim: User and group role permissions govern who can run advanced hunting queries, including queries over this Defender table.
claims.quote:
You need to be assigned permissions before you can run advanced hunting queries. You have the following options:
Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (URBAC)

claims.claim: The portal enforces unified RBAC role permissions and assignments only after the unified RBAC model is activated.
claims.quote: For the Microsoft Defender portal to start enforcing the permissions and assignments configured in your new or imported roles, you need to activate the new Microsoft Defender unified RBAC model.

claims.claim: Choose permissions is where the custom-role wizard lets the admin select required permissions.
claims.quote: On the Choose permissions page, select each of the following as needed to configure permissions for that area:

claims.where: Governance controls: Assign users and data sources
claims.claim: After choosing permissions, Assign users and data sources > Add assignment lets the admin select employees and data sources.
claims.quote:
On the Assign users and data sources page, select Add assignment.
Employees: Select Microsoft Entra security groups or individual users to assign users to the role.
Data sources: Select the Data sources drop down

claims.claim: Unless stated otherwise, unified RBAC permissions apply to supported workloads and the selected assignment data scope.
claims.quote: Unless otherwise stated, all permissions are applicable to all supported workloads and will be applied to the data scope selected during the data source and assignment stage.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery lets applications run advanced hunting queries.
claims.quote:
This method is for advanced hunting in Microsoft 365 Defender.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery

claims.claim: ThreatHunting.Read.All is a documented permission for runHuntingQuery.
claims.quote:
Delegated (work or school account) | ThreatHunting.Read.All | ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All
Application | ThreatHunting.Read.All | ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All

claims.quote: Searched: "CallActivityEvents" "permissions" "ActivityType"; site:learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr "CallActivityEvents" "permission". Read the complete v1.0 security: runHuntingQuery reference; it describes schema tables generally and does not name CallActivityEvents.
